draft.title: Leaders before the revolution
card: Louis XVI
King of France from 1774. He held absolute power but was indecisive. He often backed down when nobles or court members pushed back against reform.
Marie Antoinette
The queen, born in Austria. Many French people distrusted her as a foreigner and blamed her for court spending, which made the crown less popular.
Necker

A Swiss-born banker who served as finance minister. He borrowed heavily instead of raising taxes, and in 1781 he published accounts of the crown's finances that made them look healthier than they were.
Sieyès

A priest and writer. In his 1789 pamphlet What Is the Third Estate? he argued that the Third Estate was the true nation. Lafayette was a noble who had fought in the American Revolution and who backed reform.
draft.remember: Some leaders shaped the crisis by weakness or poor choices. Others gave the reformers ideas and support.

a.q: Why did Sieyès matter in the lead-up to the revolution?
opts: He argued the Third Estate was the true nation
He ran the crown's finances and borrowed to pay for wars
He was a noble who had fought in the American Revolution
He was the queen, blamed by the public for court spending
a.why: Sieyès wrote What Is the Third Estate?, which gave the Third Estate a case for its claim to power. Necker, not Sieyès, ran the finances, and Lafayette was the noble who had fought in America.
a.clue: Think about what Sieyès wrote in his pamphlet.

b.q: A student says Necker made the crown's money problems worse before 1789. Which fact from his time as finance minister best supports this?
opts: He borrowed heavily instead of raising taxes
He raised taxes on the Third Estate to pay for wars
He published a pamphlet calling for a new National Assembly
He fought in the American Revolution and returned to France
b.why: Necker relied on loans rather than taxes, so the debt kept growing. Raising taxes on the Third Estate is not what the card says he did. The pamphlet was Sieyès's work, and fighting in America was Lafayette's.
b.clue: Ask whether Necker paid for things with loans or with taxes.

a.best: He argued the Third Estate was the true nation

b.best: He borrowed heavily instead of raising taxes

proposal.title: Leaders before the revolution
card: The king and queen

Louis XVI, king from 1774, held absolute power but was indecisive. He often backed down when nobles resisted reform. Marie Antoinette, his Austrian-born queen, was distrusted as a foreigner and blamed for court spending.
Necker
A Swiss-born banker who served as finance minister. He borrowed heavily instead of raising taxes, and in 1781 he published accounts that made the crown's finances look healthier than they were.
Sieyès
A priest and writer. In his 1789 pamphlet What Is the Third Estate? he argued that the Third Estate was the true nation.
Lafayette
A noble who had fought for the Americans in their revolution. He returned to France as a supporter of reform and of limits on royal power.
